key_insight: Large language models can meaningfully support cancer registry abstraction, especially for simpler categorical variables, but performance drops for exact date extraction and more complex fields.
clinical_relevance: This study suggests LLMs could help speed up cancer registry workflows and reduce manual abstraction burden, while still requiring human oversight for higher-risk or highly precise data elements.
method: Evaluated 5 foundation LLMs in zero-shot mode
Abstracted 8 registry variables from clinical reports
Tested on 5,939 patients across 7 cancer types
evidence_signal: Using hospital registry data as ground truth, the best models reached around F1 0.8 for low-cardinality variables and about 0.55 exact accuracy for diagnosis/treatment dates, improving to roughly 0.85 with ±30-day tolerance.
watch_item: Real-world deployment should be cautious because exact date fields and other high-precision registry variables remain error-prone and would likely need verification before use.
paper_title: Large language models for cancer registry abstraction: a real-world evaluation across models, variables, and cancer types
